description: #341: a thin CLI bridge that calls .mcp.json servers headlessly and returns a real process exit code + JSON on stdout, so gh->MCP fallback branches become ordinary subprocesses that bkit's bash `|| Failure Path` gates and poll loops handle unmodified, and `0 results` vs `call failed` become distinct exit codes (the live search_issues silent-zero class). Acknowledged as the best long-term shape; deferred because it is a bespoke CLI duplicating the MCP client's auth/session semantics with its own token-scoping + injection surface, and is the new-tooling investment #341's minimal/additive principle rules out
remediation: revisit if the prose fallback (bounded + recorded + re-asserted, per design D13) proves insufficient in practice, or if the fallback path needs to be regression-tested outside a live agent session

description: #341: make PR-based phase-close the single close path in all three runtimes and delete the local squash-merge, so mode 1 (99% of runs) exercises the same close code as mode 3 instead of letting the cloud path rot between uses — the aetiology of D1. Rejected for now: regresses mode 1 (design close is offline + instant today, would need network + PR + CI), collides with the [skip ci] PR-title assert at 5 PRs/feature, and hard-depends on branch-protection settings invisible to git
remediation: revisit if the two-transport asymmetry produces a second D1-class incident; prerequisite is resolving [skip ci] on phase-close subjects (issue 341 section 6d)

description: #341: Cursor Cloud Agents (formerly Background Agents) are a 4th runtime. PROMOTED to first-class scope 2026-07-23 (was deferred). The original 'no bash-visible primitive' premise is partly right: the reliable Cursor-cloud signal is the hook stdin-JSON field is_background_agent (used by .cursor/hooks/preflight.sh, #75), NOT a workflow-shell env var — CURSOR_AGENT/CURSOR_REMOTE_AGENT are unconfirmed as Cursor-set. But Cursor still belongs in scope because bkit owns the seams to bridge that signal into a bash-visible env marker (the SessionStart hook or the .cursor/environment.json env block, both shipped by #75). Now a first-class Runtime 4 row with a mode-2-equivalent profile (CAN_WORKTREE/CAN_PUSH_DEV true optimistic, GH_OK probed). Held for live confirmation (verify-first): the exact detection bridge and whether the harness blocks foreground sleep (CAN_SLEEP). Until confirmed, an unmatched Cursor session falls through to unknown->least-capable+loud, so the row ships non-regressively.
remediation: folded into #341 T3 (runtime shim adds the Cursor row; detection bridges is_background_agent to an env marker via .cursor/environment.json env or a hook export); a live-confirmation of the exact bridge + sleep-block behaviour against a real Cursor Cloud Agent is owned by the terminal verification (Sub-Plan 6) before mode-4 is asserted in SC1

description: #341: mcp__github__search_issues silently returns total_count 0 for every query on a PRIVATE repo (control query included) while gh returns 39 — MCP up but returning a benign-looking wrong result on the one surface (trackers, section 6i) that has no fallback by design. Design D12 mitigates the symptom within MCP (a 0 is inconclusive; corroborate via a second MCP list_* signal or report unavailable) because bkit doctrine forbids gh for GitHub/Linear tracker ops. Whether section 6i should admit a narrow read-only gh corroboration probe on private repos is left open
remediation: revisit if MCP-internal corroboration proves unreliable; also needs the root cause diagnosed (bkit-side scope/config vs upstream MCP bug) — currently unknown

summary: TEST_VERDICT / TEST_SCOPE pass via jq --arg and accept empty silently — the counters' --argjson hard-stop has no equivalent
description: #58 explicitly out of scope. The same status-write blocks that pass the counter via --argjson (which hard-fails on an empty value: 'invalid JSON text passed to --argjson', exit 2) pass TEST_VERDICT / TEST_SCOPE via --arg, which accepts empty silently — an unsubstituted verdict writes verdict:"" into status.jsonl rather than failing the step. These are legitimately model judgments and #58 keeps verdict interpretation in the orchestrator, so this is not a counter problem; it is the same substitution assumption with a quieter failure mode. Affected sites include bkit-build.md:538/:612/:936, bkit-debug.md:400/:643/:756, bkit-ship.md:562/:625/:685.
remediation: Validate the verdict against the PASS|FAIL|CONCERNS vocabulary inside the write block (case "$V" in PASS|FAIL|CONCERNS) ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac) so an unsubstituted verdict routes to the Failure Path instead of writing an empty string into the log; or move the verdict through --argjson with an enum-validating jq filter.

summary: PRIOR_STRATEGY folds status.jsonl with ALL-runs scoping; whether a resumed run should restart the STANDARD->PIVOT->FINAL ladder was never established
description: #58 flagged but did not change this. PRIOR_STRATEGY (bkit-build.md:592 and :987, bkit-debug.md:624, bkit-ship.md:665) reads [.[] | .steps[] | select(...)] | last.strategy — .[] spans ALL runs. Verified: given a completed run that recorded PIVOT and a fresh second run with no diagnose rows of its own, the shipped read returns PIVOT; an active-run-scoped read returns empty. #58 scopes its attempt derivation to the ACTIVE run — deliberately OPPOSITE — because cross-run counting would hand a resumed workflow the previous run's attempts and starve its budget immediately (the starvation DE-25 had to fix for SOAK). Both sites now carry a comment naming the asymmetry, since it looks like a bug from either direction. What strategy actually wants was not established: a resumed run arguably should NOT restart the ladder from scratch, which would make the all-runs read correct.
remediation: Decide the intended resume semantics for strategy, then either scope the read to the active run (matching the attempt derivation) or record the cross-run behaviour as intentional in .bkit/workflows.md § Status so the asymmetry stops reading as an oversight.

summary: No CI gate runs shellcheck over .bkit/scripts/*.sh — actionlint only shellchecks run: blocks inside .github/workflows/*
description: Discovered while planning #58. The shipped shell surface (.bkit/scripts/bkit-counter-bus.sh, bkit-counter-bus-config.sh, bkit-slop-delta.sh, bkit-protect-main.sh, bkit-set-dependabot.sh, and #58's new bkit-status-fold.sh) is sourced by consumers under sh/dash/zsh but is linted by nothing: the bkit-tests-static lane runs actionlint, which shellchecks only the run: blocks inside .github/workflows/*. The SC2016 disable #58 adds to bkit-status-fold.sh (the fold blob's $w/$e/$i are jq variables, not shell) is therefore defensive for local runs only. A real POSIX-portability regression in a shipped script would land green and only surface in a consumer's shell.
remediation: Add a shellcheck -s sh step over .bkit/scripts/*.sh to the bkit-tests-static lane (and the .bkit/templates/.bkit/scripts/*.sh sources). Scope to the shipped scripts, not the whole repo, and pin the shellcheck version the way actionlint is pinned.

summary: The 'start a new run?' test keys on the last run overall, not the last run of THIS workflow — an interleaved debug run can silently reset a resuming build's attempt budget
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. bkit-build.md:335 tests (.[-1] // {}) — the last folded run of ANY workflow — to decide whether to append a fresh workflow-started row. build and debug write to the SAME docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl. So if a debug run interleaves and completes between two build invocations, a resuming build sees .[-1].workflow == 'debug', appends a fresh workflow-started, and starts a NEW active run — resetting its attempt budget. #58 makes active-run scoping the basis of every counter, which promotes this from latent to load-bearing: it is Defect 3 (fresh budget on resume) through a side door, reachable via the exact build->debug->build path the feature governs. A lock exists at bkit-build.md:143; whether it excludes the interleave is NOT established. #58 characterises current behaviour in tests/counter-derive.bats (T2.10) so the dependence is visible rather than latent, but does not change the boundary.
remediation: Decide the intended run-boundary semantics and key the test on the last run OF THE SAME WORKFLOW (e.g. [.[] | select(.workflow==$w)] | last) rather than .[-1], or establish and document that the bkit-build.md:143 lock makes the interleave impossible. Belongs with #209's status.jsonl substrate, not with #58's control-flow slice. Read T2.10's characterisation assertion first — it records what today actually does.

summary: debug-run-tests writes its step-done row with no commit (KN-26 removed it), so NORMAL_ATTEMPT's row counting depends transitively on Steps 4/5/6 advancing parentSha
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. #58 counts step-done rows and dedups on 'S {workflow} {step} {parentSha} {at}'. build-run-tests commits --allow-empty per attempt (bkit-build.md:939), so its parentSha advances by itself. debug-run-tests does NOT (bkit-debug.md:396 reads 'Update status:' with no commit — the only step-done-writing step in debug without one). That asymmetry is KN-26's remediation: a chore(...) commit as branch HEAD makes the Vercel-ignore regex skip the preview, CI demotes to partial, integration/Playwright are skipped, and the run reports conclusion=success with no coverage. So NORMAL_ATTEMPT's attempts stay distinct only via Steps 4/5/6's commits (bkit-debug.md:573/:646/:707) advancing parentSha, plus the dedup key's 'at' second. Whether debug-run-tests SHOULD regain a commit — making its row counting self-sufficient — is a real design question that collides with KN-26 and must not be settled by an implementer applying #58's per-site shape. #58 pins the current shape with a corpus audit (T2.6) that requires each counted step to either commit in-block or sit on a commented transitive-exemption list.
remediation: If debug-run-tests's transitive parentSha dependency proves fragile, resolve it WITHOUT re-adding a chore(...) commit — e.g. amend the dedup key, or have the step commit under a subject the Vercel-ignore regex does not match. Any change must be reviewed against KN-26's full failure chain first. Do not simply delete the T2.6 exemption entry.

summary: The 5 close-workflow counter emitters declare counterName DESIGN_ATTEMPT/PLAN_ATTEMPT/BUILD_ATTEMPT/... but #58 derives counterValue from the workflow-started count — the pairing is unverified
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. #58's T7.1 replaces --argjson counterValue 1 (a hardcoded literal labelled model-self-report) with a fold-derived all-runs count of workflow-started events for that workflow, and flips counterSource to shell-bus. That makes the VALUE honest — it is a real number the shell counted. Whether that number is what each emitter's declared counterName means is a separate question #58 does not adjudicate: the names (DESIGN_ATTEMPT, PLAN_ATTEMPT, BUILD_ATTEMPT, ...) suggest an invocation index, which the workflow-started count is, but this was asserted rather than established against #234's schema intent. Flagged so the value/name pairing is not quietly assumed correct by the next reader of stats.jsonl.
remediation: Settle alongside #234's counterSource enum question ('derived' vs 'shell-bus' — which names the transport rather than the provenance). Confirm each emitter's counterName denotes an invocation index; if any denotes something else, either rename it or derive a different value for that emitter. #234 owns the schema.

summary: periodic bkit-analysis pass summarising transport-fallback frequency against GH_OK=false runs
description: #341 OQ5 (design, recorded not-adopted): a recurring reader that aggregates status.jsonl transport-fallback rows against runtime-resolved GH_OK=false runs to surface how often the gh->MCP fallback fires in mode 3. Out of scope for #341 — it is a new analysis feature, not part of the runtime-execution change. Design D25 already gives the rows a mechanical reader inside the Close Workflow (the part that belongs to #341); the aggregation/reporting layer is the additive extra.
remediation: revisit if transport-fallback frequency becomes an operational concern post-ship; a new bkit-analysis reader over the existing status.jsonl rows, no new artifact type

summary: mode-tuned concurrency pacing for subagent fan-out vs the shared-account rate budget on the claude.ai runner
description: #341 §6g (N2, deferred): the claude.ai runner shares an account-level rate budget, so a phase's subagent fan-out can hit shared-account rate limits that modes 1/2 do not. Deferred in the issue as 'revisit only if hit'; the fix would be mode-tuned concurrency pacing (throttle fan-out when RUNTIME=3). Out of scope for #341's minimal/additive runtime-execution change.
remediation: revisit only if a live mode-3 run (WS-16) actually hits the shared-account rate ceiling; fix would pace fan-out concurrency on RUNTIME=3

summary: optional dev-located roadmap.md status write from build/debug closes for live between-ship status
description: #380 v1 commits the mechanical roadmap-status block where each phase already commits (dev for design/plan/ship; feat for build/debug, reaching dev at ship), so dev's docs/roadmap.md status can lag for issues sitting in build/debug until the next design/plan/ship close — the tracker bkit:* labels remain the live-phase authority (loud banner). A future option adds a dev-located write under ship's dev-lock idiom from build/debug closes so dev's board reflects build/debug phases in real time, at the cost of adding dev-writes to two workflows that today never touch dev.
remediation: revisit if between-ship build/debug status on dev proves load-bearing; would reuse ship's dev-lock + git -C REPO_ROOT dev-commit idiom + a STRAY-guard widen in the build/debug closes

summary: persist the roadmap fold's frontier snapshot (or a roadmap.jsonl event log) if #260 needs durable cross-tick sensing
description: #380 builds the sense primitive as a deterministic in-memory fold (bkit-roadmap-fold.sh over tracker labels + status.jsonl) that #260's tick-step-1 can call directly; it deliberately does NOT persist a new roadmap.jsonl event log (rejected for v1 as duplicating status.jsonl's per-FID phase events, adding compaction machinery, and contesting the owner's 'must be docs/roadmap.md'). If #260's timeline pulls in a need for durable, replayable cross-tick frontier history, promote the fold snapshot to a persisted structured artifact at that point.
remediation: revisit when #260 is designed; if durable cross-tick sensing is required, persist the fold snapshot as a path-scoped merge=union ledger with compaction, reusing status.jsonl's envelope + TS-source-of-truth-mirrored-as-jq pattern

summary: first-bootstrap content-preservation when a consumer already hand-authored docs/roadmap.md with non-marker freeform content
description: Scope-check OPTIONAL (plan-scope-check-1.md #1): the fold bootstrap (Task 3) creates empty machine blocks + banner + empty ## Backlog / Ideas, and the Edge Cases table only covers missing/mangled markers on a file already in the new format. A consumer who hand-authored docs/roadmap.md BEFORE adopting #380 has freeform content and no markers; the plan does not specify whether that content is preserved (e.g. wrapped as Backlog) or orphaned/clobbered, brushing against SC#5 (consumer-owned, never overwrite). Low blast radius for the bkit repo itself (no docs/roadmap.md exists here, so the WS-6 dogfood wont exercise it) but a real consumer path.
remediation: if pulled in: specify first-bootstrap preserve-vs-clobber of pre-existing non-marker content (wrap it under ## Backlog / Ideas rather than clobber) in Task 3 and add a bats row (tests/roadmap-fold.bats) asserting pre-existing non-marker content survives the first fold

summary: promote the remaining ship git/CI mechanics (base classify, integrate, re-validate, path-scoped ledger commit) from prose into .bkit/scripts alongside the merge gate
description: 384 adopts a tiered carrier: only the merge gate (the one rule whose failure is unrecoverable) becomes an executable .bkit/scripts/bkit-ship-gate.sh with bats coverage; base classification, integration, re-validation and the ledger commit stay prose constrained by a vitest markdown-invariant test. Both the pragmatic and optimal-tradeoff lenses independently identified full kernel extraction as the correct two-year shape, and it was rejected for this cycle only because it would design function boundaries against semantics still being decided in the same change, and because it creates a second source of truth plus a version-skew hazard between installed scripts and rendered markdown. Once 384 lands, the contract is defined and the extraction becomes mechanical.
remediation: after 384 ships and one or two ship cycles have run against the new shape, extract ship_base_is_current / ship_integrate / ship_revalidate / ship_book_commit into the existing bkit-ship-gate.sh module with .bats coverage and install/uninstall manifest wiring; reduce bkit-ship.md to source-and-call orchestration

summary: promote the status.jsonl step-set hole detector from a fail-open advisory to a blocking gate once the delta baseline is clean
description: 384 ships the hole detector as a fail-open advisory with a pinned watermark and a delta report, matching the bkit comply rollout, because the existing corpus is 25-65% holey across app-gether-life and visitfrasercoast-com and a day-one aggregate gate would emit hundreds of findings and be muted within a week. The expected step set is derived from bkit-ship.md rather than a parallel table, so the contract tracks the workflow automatically. Promotion to a blocking gate is the intended end state but requires the delta baseline to be clean first.
remediation: once the delta against the pinned watermark stays clean for a release across the consumer repos, flip the detector to exit non-zero on new holes and wire it into bkit check

summary: remove ships writable checkout of feat/{FID} entirely except inside the B2 conflict window, so bookkeeping-never-moves-the-head becomes unreachable rather than remembered
description: The risk-premortem lens proposed making the invariant structural: ship runs from the dev tree plus gh API calls and never holds a writable feat/{FID} checkout outside B2. Rejected for 384 because the evidence inverts its premise - B2 (same-line doc collisions on long-lived branches) is the common case, not the escape hatch, so the approach concentrates all remaining worktree usage in the path exercised most and tested least while every other path loses its checkout and its diagnosability. Its two strongest findings (scope Step 12 removal to run-created worktrees, and state the invariant as push timing rather than tree location) are absorbed into 384 as decisions. Revisit only after 384s gate has run in production and if B2 gains real conflict-resolution coverage.
remediation: if revisited: sequence after the merge gate exists and is proven, scope Step 12 to ownership first, keep the push-timing formulation, and add a vitest invariant asserting no git commit or git push targets feat/{FID} outside the B2 block

summary: define a recovery path for a shipped-but-wrong workflow change - consumers pin @cbartens/bkit and receive workflows on bkit upgrade, with no per-workflow revert
description: Surfaced by the 384 risk premortem as a cross-cutting gap rather than a 384 defect. Consumers receive .bkit/workflows via bkit upgrade at a pinned package version; there is no mechanism to revert a single workflow file to a prior known-good version without downgrading the whole package, which also reverts unrelated fixes. If a new ship merge gate is wrong, the recovery path for three consumer repos is currently undefined. 384 mitigates locally with a single logged override (BKIT_SHIP_GATE_OVERRIDE recorded as a status.jsonl row), but that is a per-run escape, not a rollback.
remediation: design a per-workflow pin or revert affordance for bkit upgrade (e.g. a .bkitignore-style per-file version pin, or bkit upgrade --revert <workflow> restoring the prior canonicalHash), and document the recovery runbook in docs/deployments.md

summary: Sub-Plan 6/T16 Manual Verification Steps 1-4 (mode-1 laptop e2e, mode-3 claude.ai session, mode-2 CI-runner trigger, dev branch-protection/auto-delete-head-branches admin confirmation) are unreachable from a single non-interactive build-execute subagent turn and remain deliberately unchecked
description: All buildable/automatable T16 scope is complete and green (row 15 prose-audit test passing 8/8, batch mirror regen via `pnpm bkit upgrade` installing `.bkit/scripts/bkit-runtime.sh` for the first time, the T14/T15-discovered `runtime-resolved-row-never-emitted-step1` gap fixed by wiring `bkit_runtime_row` into Step 2 of all five phase workflows, full local gate suite green). The remaining 4 Manual Verification steps are, by the design's own honest limit (D3), reachable ONLY via genuine live sessions: Step 1 requires actually running all five phases + bkit-auto to completion on the laptop against a real FID (a multi-hour, multi-PR undertaking out of scope for a single sub-plan-6 build turn); Step 2 requires an actual claude.ai (mode-3, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true) browser session, which this environment cannot open; Step 3 requires triggering the CI event/label path and observing a real GH-Actions runner; Step 4 requires GitHub repo-admin dashboard access to confirm branch-protection + auto-delete-head-branches settings, which this agent does not hold. This mirrors Sub-Plan 5's precedent (Manual Verification Step 5, debug-egress loudness) of leaving a live-only step deliberately unchecked rather than fabricating completion.
remediation: Human (cbartens) runs the four Manual Verification steps directly: (1) a real `/bkit-auto`-driven laptop run of a throwaway FID through all five phases, confirming mint-path/local-close unchanged and no `[skip ci]` in landed bodies; (2) a real claude.ai cloud session running the same phases, confirming adopt-or-mint (no worktree), no `git checkout dev`, and settling the three named live residuals (sleep block-vs-error, which MCP server + GH_BKIT_TOKEN in-sandbox, push_files/PR-close reject-vs-clobber); (3) a CI event/label dispatch on the GH-Actions runner confirming RUNTIME=2; (4) a `dev` branch-protection + auto-delete-head-branches confirmation in the GitHub repo settings dashboard (or `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/dev/protection`). Once run, check the corresponding boxes in `docs/plans/202607/341-three-runtimes-plan-6.md` Manual Verification section.

summary: Marker-primary FID reorder (D9) elevates untrusted PR-body input for filesystem path construction with no documented slug validation
description: docs/plans/202607/logs/341-three-runtimes/build-challenge.md finding F4: bkit-auto.md steps 9-10 (D9 reorder) make the PR-body marker <!-- bkit:fid={FID} --> the PRIMARY FID source, ahead of the feat/-derived branch fallback. Per docs/security.md section CI Auto-Route Trust, the PR body is only collaborator-trusted (triage/write, not commit-signed). FID subsequently flows into filesystem paths (docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/..., .worktrees/{FID}) with no documented validation that it is a bare slug (no / or ..), so a marker like bkit:fid=../../elsewhere could redirect status/worktree writes outside the intended log directory. Classed architectural (touches the FID-resolution contract consumed across all five phase workflows, not a single mechanical file fix) -- deferred rather than remediated in this build-challenge pass per protocol (architectural findings are not fixed inline).
remediation: Validate the parsed FID against a strict slug allowlist (e.g. ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$, rejecting / and ..) before it builds any path, in the same step it is extracted (bkit-auto.md step 9). Record the constraint alongside the marker-trust text in docs/security.md section CI Auto-Route Trust. Apply consistently across every workflow that consumes FID for path construction.

summary: Marker-primary FID reorder (D9) elevates untrusted PR-body input for filesystem path construction with no documented slug validation
description: Resolved: bkit-auto.md now asserts a strict slug allowlist at every FID exit point — step 9 github (^[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$), linear (^[a-z]+-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$), no-tracker (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$), and the step-10 branch-derive fallback (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$) — rejecting / . .. and shell metacharacters before {FID} reaches any path or downstream dispatch. Constraint recorded in docs/security.md section CI Auto-Route Trust; behaviour+presence test bkit-auto-fid-guard.test.ts (39 cases).
remediation: Slug allowlist enforced at resolution site per docs/security.md CI Auto-Route Trust.

summary: CLOSED — 2 of the 4 manual-verification items resolved without a live session; the other 2 re-filed narrowly (see 341-live-run-verification-mode-1-and-mode-3)
description: Original row bundled 4 items. Resolved here: (a) dev branch-protection / auto-delete-head-branches admin confirmation — auto-delete-head-branches ENABLED on cbartens/bkit via the REST API; branch-protection and ruleset APIs return 403 (unavailable for a private repo on this plan), so no rule can block the autonomous merge here — both recorded in docs/deployments.md rather than deferred. (b) mode-2 CI-runner e2e — no longer a distinct path: RUNTIME=actions resolves CAN_WORKTREE/CAN_PUSH_DEV/CAN_SLEEP all true, byte-identical to RUNTIME=local at every call site, and the classification itself is asserted in tests/bkit-runtime.bats. Remaining: mode-1 laptop e2e and mode-3 claude.ai session.
remediation: Superseded by 341-live-run-verification-mode-1-and-mode-3.

summary: A real /bkit-design or /bkit-plan close has not been run on a laptop (mode 1) or in a claude.ai cloud session (mode 3) since the close path was restructured
description: The restructure makes CAN_PUSH_DEV=true replay the pre-change local block verbatim (local squash-merge, docs({FID}): {phase} DONE bkit [skip ci], direct dev push, worktree teardown), so mode 1 and mode 2 execute the code path that already worked. That is asserted structurally (commit subjects diffed byte-for-byte against dev; full suite green) but not yet exercised end-to-end. The PR-merge branch (mode 3) has no non-live coverage at all — it needs an actual claude.ai session to confirm the PR create/merge, the auto-delete-head-branches cleanup, and the adopt-mode worktree skip.
remediation: Before merge: run one real /bkit-design or /bkit-plan cycle on the laptop and confirm the close lands docs({FID}): ... DONE bkit [skip ci] on dev with no CI run dispatched, and that ship completes with a dirty dev tree (the AHEAD_NON_SKIP path). After merge: run one phase from a claude.ai cloud session and confirm the PR-path close.

summary: Do not fold #384 into #341 — sequence ship redesign after runtime-aware close lands
description: #384 (Path A read-only resume / Path B integrate-then-revalidate, one capstone gate, bookkeeping on the dev tree) layers on #341 rather than conflicting. #341 makes ship runtime-aware (where the tree is, whether RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES); #384 makes ship head-stable (what may move the PR head). One interaction: #384 says bookkeeping never rides the feature branch — status.jsonl/ship artifacts go to the dev tree from Step 1 — but a cloud runtime cannot write the dev tree. Express that as: write to the dev tree when RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=true, else to the current branch. Folding #384 into #341 would re-open the local-path byte-identity question this PR closed.
remediation: Land #341 first. Then design/plan #384 with the RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES-conditioned bookkeeping rule already available.

summary: GitHub merge queue (rebase onto base, CI on merge_group, server-side merge if green) is unavailable to bkit consumers — private + non-Enterprise; would require a merge_group trigger in every consumer ci.yml
description: #384 Out-of-Scope mirror. A GitHub merge queue would make the merge gate server-side (rebase onto base, run CI on the merge_group event, auto-merge if green) and remove the head-movement race bkit-ship-gate.sh exists to close. Unavailable: bkit consumer repos (app-gether-life, visitfrasercoast-com) are private and on a non-Enterprise plan; merge_group is an Enterprise/Beta feature gated behind plan tier. Adopting it would require every consumer ci.yml to add a merge_group trigger and the repos to upgrade their plan — a cross-consumer policy change, not a ship-workflow decision.
remediation: revisit only if the consumer plan tier changes (private repos gain merge queue access); record the plan-tier gate in docs/deployments.md alongside the merge-gate contract when revisited

summary: Required status checks on dev via bkit-protect-main.sh (closing the UI hand-merge path) — separable additive cross-consumer policy with its own plan-tier question; deferred from #384 ship gate
description: #384 Out-of-Scope mirror. bkit-protect-main.sh already makes bkit-tests-check the sole required check on main. Extending required-status-checks enforcement to dev (so a human cannot UI-merge a PR whose capstone is not green, closing the gap bkit-ship-gate.sh closes on the agent path) is a separable additive policy. It has its own plan-tier question: branch protection on private repos is plan-gated (the REST protection/ruleset APIs return 403 on cbartens/bkit today — see docs/deployments.md § Autonomous phase-close prerequisites), so the enforcement cannot be verified mechanically on every consumer. Out of scope for #384 because the agent-driven gate (bkit-ship-gate.sh) is the load-bearing assertion; UI-merge prevention is defence-in-depth, not the contract.
remediation: future issue: extend bkit-protect-main.sh to dev (or a ruleset) and document the plan-tier prerequisite; pair with per-workflow-rollback-path-for-shipped-bkit-workflow-changes if that affordance lands first

summary: Mode-3 (cloud, RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=false) BOOK_ROOT live-verification is not exercised in #384 E2E validation — both validated paths are local-mode (RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=true). Prose contract mechanically asserted by Tier-2 invariant (bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts BOOK_ROOT conditional presence check, 14/14 GREEN) and ship-failure-path.bats case 2. Live E2E deferred to first mode-3 ship run.
reason: Mode-3 cloud runtime (RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=false) is not available in the build session — requires a cloud agent (Claude Code cloud / Cursor cloud) executing a ship workflow. The #341 three-runtimes feature introduced the RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES flag but its live verification is itself still OPEN.

summary: Second /bkit-audit synthesis correlation rule (derived-divergence-candidate) joining derived-data dual-source-writer with reliability unchecked-write on one subject — deliberately not shipped in 4.11.0
description: Pass-4 design out-of-scope mirror. The A4 correlation rule table ships exactly one rule (silent-corruption-candidate). derived-data emits a dual-source-writer signal in 4.11.0 that no rule consumes, so the signal is emitted-but-unjoined. A second rule is new probe behaviour rather than reconciliation, and one rule already proves the mechanism and exercises the unevaluable coverage path on the bkit dogfood run.
remediation: after one real /bkit-audit run has produced a dual-source-writer signal, add one row to the rule table in bkit-audit.md Step 6 plus the derived copy in bkit-audit-synthesise.md; the four-way parity assert keeps the two copies honest

summary: The /bkit-audit severity x class matrix was designed at 11 lenses; at 18 it flattens — maintainability alone carries 7 lenses — and WS-D (#207) makes it worse
description: Pass-4 design out-of-scope mirror. 18 lenses map onto 7 finding classes, so the matrix loses discriminating power: architecture, debt, dead-code, docs-drift, logic-dupe, ui-ux and reference-signal all land in maintainability. Accepted for 4.11.0; the per-class appendix is the escape valve for a human reader. Introducing a sub-class axis is a report-shape change, out of scope for a reconciliation pass.
remediation: decide during WS-D (#207) design, which adds the web-product lens family and compounds the flattening; either accept the flat matrix permanently or introduce a sub-class axis once, not per workstream

summary: No audit-{token} skills exist in the public registry, so /bkit-audit Step 4 (skill install) will mostly no-op — whether bkit authors a minimal seed set is unowned
description: Pass-4 design out-of-scope mirror, carried unresolved from Pass 3. The stack-detect + skill-install enrichment model is the mechanism by which stack-specific depth reaches the stack-agnostic lens prompts, but the registry has no audit-{token} skills to install. The non-gating posture absorbs this and the audit runs to full strength on universal probes regardless, so it is a latent value gap rather than a blocker. Pass 3 routed this to docs/pending.md, which no longer exists — hence the orphan.
remediation: after the first real /bkit-audit runs, decide whether bkit authors a minimal seed set of audit-{token} skills or leaves the surface to the community; either way record the decision rather than carrying it as a design open question a fourth time

summary: Reconciler/sweeper to recover a ship displaced out of the depth-1 GHA concurrency queue
description: GHA holds exactly one pending run per concurrency group; a third concurrent ship displaces the pending second. That PR stays green, open and merge-ready but never ships, and the displaced run executes no step so no bkit-authored notice, comment, label or ledger row can exist for it. #397 restates requirement 1 as met for N=2 only and accepts the N>=3 hole this cycle, because the allowlist ship discriminator removes the dominant eviction source (green dev CI entering the ship lane). The automated fix is an idempotent reconciler: sweep for green bkit:auto PRs with no in-flight ship and re-dispatch, riding the post-merge dev CI trigger #363 adds (which fires exactly when the ship lane frees).
remediation: future issue after #397 lands: bump cloud job permissions to actions: write; cap the sweeper hard (max one dispatch per sweep, reuse #363's MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS bounding); make the admission probe and the sweep predicate call ONE shared implementation, not two similar gh run list invocations; keep the predicate stack-agnostic (workflow filename, never a consumer-editable CI display name). Belongs with #260's single-flight/idempotent-dispatch substrate.

summary: Split bkit-cloud.yml into a light router plus a single-trigger-surface executor workflow — the deferred target shape for multi-producer dispatch
description: #397 records this as the right long-term shape and rejects it for this cycle. bkit-cloud.yml keeps both trigger surfaces but becomes a router (checkout + resolve, ending in gh workflow run bkit-cloud-run.yml -f phase -f fid -f arg); the new executor has ONE trigger surface with ONE payload shape, so its concurrency group is a literal string and the cross-surface same-FID gap stops existing rather than being closed. It is also the natural dispatch primitive #260 (milestone workstreams) and #324 (audit findings) both want to consume: adding a producer becomes adding a caller, not editing a concurrency expression. Rejected now as net-new shipped infra (new workflow file, manifest entry, template, advisory, actions: write bump, two-hop latency, doubled Actions run count) for a problem two expressions plus a resolver job cover.
remediation: revisit when #260 and #324 add the second and third dispatch producers; at that point #397's expression work becomes the thing this replaces. A dropped or 403 re-dispatch is a silent no-op for a whole phase, so the router needs its own dispatch-verify.

summary: External cross-runner mutex (orphan git ref or issue-label compare-and-swap) as a real distributed single-flight lock
description: #397 rejects this for its own scope. The file locks (.bkit/.dev.lock, docs/plans/*/logs/{FID}/.lock) are gitignored and runner-local, so they arbitrate nothing across GHA runners. A primitive that does survive would be a compare-and-swap on a dedicated orphan ref (git push origin <sha>:refs/bkit-locks/ship-global — GitHub ref creation is server-atomic) or an issue-label CAS tolerating the 422 as lock-held, with age-based stale reaping mirroring today's 30-min-idle rule. It closes both gaps without depending on any inferred GHA behaviour. Rejected because it introduces a DURABLE state surface whose lock survives a hard-killed runner with no guaranteed reaper (an if: always() step can still be skipped on hard cancellation) — a worse blast radius than an ephemeral file lock that vanishes with the VM — and because it would leave two independent lock layers to reconcile.
remediation: revisit only if #260's single-flight lock / leader election requirement lands first and wants to share a primitive; design the reaper before the acquirer.

summary: With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY both set, one bkit-cloud run launches two agents that both dispatch /bkit-auto against the same PR
description: The claude and opencode jobs are additive by design and documented as such in the bkit-cloud.yml header: both fire on the same event when both secrets are present. They are ONE run, so workflow-level concurrency cannot separate them by construction — a ship-global lane delivers one ship RUN at a time, not one ship AGENT at a time. Two agents then race on the same feat/{FID} branch and the same PR, backstopped only by gh pr merge --match-head-commit. #397 leaves this exactly as today: its job-level FID lanes are suffixed per agent (-claude / -opencode) precisely so the additive contract is not silently converted into a queue with its own eviction hazard. Pre-existing, not introduced by #397, and simultaneously an intended feature and an unarbitrated same-FID collision.
remediation: future issue: decide whether additive dual-agent execution is still wanted post-#397; if yes, scope it to non-mutating phases or give the two agents disjoint worktrees; if no, make the jobs mutually exclusive at the secret-gate step rather than via a shared concurrency group.

summary: Nothing detects that the cloud egress allowlist pasted into a Claude/Cursor dashboard is stale relative to what bkit generates
description: cloud.md renders a paste block a human copies into a vendor dashboard. When bkit's derived host set changes (new provider, new MCP host) the dashboard keeps the old value and the only symptom is an opaque harness timeout on the model call, not a network error. No surface can compare intended to actual because the allowlist lives in a web UI. #381 ships a stable fingerprint line in the paste block as the cheap half of the mitigation; detection is out of scope.
remediation: future issue: have the cloud bootstrap hook echo the expected allowlist fingerprint (and optionally probe reachability of one provider host) so a mismatch is visible in the cloud run log

summary: OpenCode curl/wget allowlist is a command substring glob, so an allowlisted domain in a query param or header defeats the host check Cursor now enforces
description: injectOpencodeNetworkCurlAllows writes permission.bash entries of the form 'curl *{base}*' (bkit-modules.ts:1706-1714). OpenCode's permission model is a command glob, so 'curl https://evil.tld/?x=z.ai' matches and is allowed, while the Cursor hook rejects it (host-parsed since #394) and Claude has no shell curl gate at all. #381 widens the base list and therefore widens this asymmetry; it documents the weaker guarantee in .bkit/providers.md rather than fixing it, because OpenCode exposes no URL-host permission primitive.
remediation: future issue: revisit if OpenCode gains a host-based permission primitive or a pre-tool hook comparable to Cursor beforeShellExecution; until then keep the limitation stated in providers.md

summary: One generated allowlist artifact read at runtime by all three IDE surfaces is blocked by the Claude and OpenCode permission schemas, not by bkit design
description: The theoretical ideal is a single JSON artifact (tooling defaults + all registry hosts + consumer allowed-domains) that every surface reads at runtime, collapsing BKIT_SHIPPED_NETWORK_DOMAINS, the Cursor hook list and the WebFetch allow entries into reads of one file. Cursor already works this way via .cursor/allowlist.json. Claude permissions.allow requires a literal WebFetch(domain:...) string per host and OpenCode permission.bash requires a literal command glob per host, neither has a file-reference primitive, so the work would land for 1 of 3 surfaces. Recorded so it is not re-proposed without re-discovering the constraint.
remediation: revisit only if Claude Code or OpenCode ships a file-referenced permission source; most of the maintenance win is already captured by deriving the source list in #381

summary: The opencode provider key set is still mirrored by hand into four lists plus two doc tables, each held together only by a keep-in-sync comment
description: #381 removes the domain-list duplication but not the key-set duplication: OPENCODE_PROVIDER_DEFAULTS (bkit-modules.ts:1397) is mirrored by OPENCODE_PROVIDERS + OPENCODE_PROVIDER_ALIASES (bkit-cli.ts:43-74), OPENCODE_PROVIDER_COLUMN (bkit-install.ts:320), EFFORT_COLUMN_FOR_PROVIDER (bkit-install.ts:436), and the Models tables in .bkit/prompts.md and .bkit/providers.md. bkit-cli.ts:40 carries the same 'keep in sync with ...' comment pattern #381 exists to remove, and no test asserts key-set parity. Out of scope for #381, which is scoped to egress hosts.
remediation: future issue: derive the CLI allowlist and the display/effort column maps from the registry moved to .bkit/src/bkit-registry.ts by #381, and add a key-set parity test over every mirror

summary: No lens in the /bkit-audit 18 covers API-contract conformance — deferred in Pass 2, never re-recorded, and invisible once Pass 2 became historical
description: Pass 2 (bar-199-audit-workflow-design.md) deferred an api-contracts lens on the argument that structural source probes have poor signal-to-noise without a live surface to diff against. Pass 3 said nothing about it and Pass 4 folded no probe for it, so the 18-lens inventory silently has no coverage of published-interface breakage, schema drift between producer and consumer, or endpoint contract regressions. The defer is still the right call — the gap is that the RATIONALE stopped being visible the moment Passes 2 and 3 were reclassified as historical and the Pass-4 doc became the sole input to /bkit-plan. That is the same failure shape that lost the WS-1..WS-8 decomposition when sub-issues 187-193 and 208 were deleted.
remediation: do NOT add a lens without first reading this row — it has now been deferred twice on the same signal-to-noise argument. Candidate home is WS-E (#83) once runtime evidence exists and a real surface can be diffed, or a conditional lens gated on a new hasPublicApi flag authored in WS-C. Not 4.11.0.

summary: No lens in the /bkit-audit 18 covers rate limiting / abuse throttling — deferred in Pass 2, never re-recorded
description: Pass 2 deferred a rate-limiting lens alongside api-contracts on the same argument. Pass 4 carries no probe for request throttling, quota enforcement, backoff on retry paths, or abuse surfaces, and the security lens (B9) is chartered to hunt permissive holes in auth, validation, secrets and data exposure rather than request-rate policy. Verified absent under every synonym (rate-limit, throttl, quota, backoff, abuse). The defer stands: detecting a MISSING rate limit needs request-path modelling that a static grep-shaped lens does not do, and a false negative here reads as a clean security pass.
remediation: candidate homes are WS-E (#83, once a live surface can be probed) or an amendment to security (B9) — but only with a probe that can distinguish absent-limit from limit-enforced-at-a-layer-not-in-this-repo, otherwise it emits confident false negatives on exactly the class it exists to catch. Not 4.11.0.

summary: derived-data (C3) absorbs only the CONSISTENCY half of Pass-2 deferred caching lens — TTL, invalidation, stampede and key-cardinality remain uncovered by all 18
description: Pass 2 deferred a caching lens. Pass 4 introduces derived-data (C3, gated on hasDerivedStore), which covers cache CONSISTENCY: single-authoritative-writer, every source-mutation path updating the derived store, and whether any test or store constraint asserts the two agree. It does NOT cover cache CORRECTNESS or EFFICIENCY: TTL policy, invalidation strategy, stampede / thundering-herd protection, or key-cardinality blowup. The risk is a reader treating the Pass-2 caching defer as fully resolved because a cache-shaped lens now exists, when only one half was absorbed — the partial absorption is easy to mistake for a complete one.
remediation: if the caching half is wanted, it is an amendment to derived-data (C3) rather than a new lens — same hasDerivedStore gate, same subject identity — but it changes the lens from a consistency derivation into a policy scan, so decide deliberately rather than by accretion. Not 4.11.0.

summary: main branch excluded from the bkit-cloud workflow_run trigger — a documented REVERSAL of #363 pivot-comment D-final, which settled the branch filter as [feat/**, fix/**, dev, main]
description: #363's pivot comment (2026-07-22) D-final explicitly listed 'verify at both dev (post-merge) and main (post dev->main promotion)' with a routing table and diff both including main. The plan (v3/v4) moved main to Out of Scope instead, and this build ships without it. Rationale: the issue's own open item 3 never resolved 'routing on main only works if the promotion commit carries the marker; bkit has no consumer-facing dev->main promotion workflow, so confirm where that commit is authored (may be out of bkit's control for some consumers)' -- with no bkit-authored promotion commit to thread bkit [auto route] onto, a main trigger would be gated shut by construction for exactly the consumers it targets. A follow-up comment (2026-07-29) additionally locked bkit:auto as dev-only by policy: dev->main promotion and any merge into main always requires explicit human interaction, matching the existing hard-stop after Ship (docs/comparison.md).
remediation: revisit only if/when a bkit-authored dev->main promotion workflow exists that could carry the bkit [auto route] marker on the promotion commit; until then main stays workflow_dispatch-only (manual)

summary: MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS cap is enforced from status.jsonl on origin/dev, a file the dispatched /bkit-debug session itself has contents:write to rewrite — the cap is self-resettable by the principal it bounds
description: bkit-cloud.yml documents MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS=3 as a cost/security control bounding a stuck dev/fix/** feedback loop, but the counter it reads (dev-dispatch rows in docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl on origin/dev) is the same file every dispatched /bkit-debug session legitimately edits every run, with contents:write. Any actor or malfunctioning/prompt-injected agent that can push to dev can rewrite or drop those rows, silently restoring the remaining-attempts budget to 3 and continuing the failure->debug->push->failure cycle indefinitely. The fail-closed push-verification added for #363 P6 protects only against under-counting from lost pushes, not against an authorized rewrite.
remediation: Derive the count from a source the dispatched session cannot rewrite — e.g. gh run list --workflow bkit-cloud.yml filtered by FID, or an append-only tracker comment/label written with a token the dispatched session does not hold — or minimally cross-check the file-derived count against gh api run history and take the maximum before dispatching. This is a new counter architecture, not a mechanical patch, so it was deferred rather than attempted in the build-challenge-remediate pass.
